# Discussion {#sec-article-04-discussion}

## What the relative analyses add

The principal added information is the distinction between widespread screening concern, relative receiving priority and source pressure. Spatial association contributes additional evidence rather than defining the entire management map. An attainment-oriented result can indicate that many units require attention while offering little guidance about their relative configuration. Receptor quintiles and local association maps retain that configuration, and the zoning translation preserves the proportion affected within each administrative unit. Their usefulness therefore concerns the organization of investigations and control discussions, not a new interpretation of the numerical air quality standards.

The result is consistent with the rationale for data-derived air quality regionalization described by Liu et al. (2018), Akhtar and Han (2026) and the recent time-series macroregions of Morawiec et al. (2026). The latter uses monitoring-series similarity, while the present clustering uses four simulated summary indicators. Our evidence is more restricted: it concerns patterns within an existing dispersion scenario, rather than improved prediction from a newly trained air quality model. The externally reported accuracy improvements of those studies should not be attributed to the present procedure. Here, the explicit neighbourhood sensitivity is part of the contribution because it shows where a proposed management boundary depends on an analytical choice.

## Why an associative split is not a control limit

Local emissions contribute to a concentration field that also depends on transport, source geometry, release conditions and meteorology. A statistical split of local mass or density consequently cannot isolate the concentration effect of adding one tonne at a specific source. The unequal spatial-test performance across concentration targets and the spread of fitted cutoffs illustrate that limitation. Fixed 100 t/year screening and empirical cutoffs can be compared as descriptive tools, but neither should be converted into a universal municipal emission allowance through this analysis alone.

For operational control scenarios, the next step is to perturb documented source activities and evaluate the resulting concentration changes at the receiving regions. Clappier et al. (2017) emphasizes the different purposes of attribution and sensitivity. In the present primary-particle scenario, source-group outputs are useful for selecting which activities to investigate, while temporal changes require additional model calculations. A strong received contribution is therefore a starting point for source-specific assessment, not an automatic statement about the reduction obtainable from a control measure.

## Interpretation under model and support uncertainty

The observed–modelled discrepancy remains a central limitation. Relative classification can retain information when a field has a broad multiplicative bias, but it is not protected against spatially varying errors or incorrect source timing. The difference between modelled and observed diurnal patterns motivates checking operation schedules alongside mixing conditions, rather than fitting emission multipliers directly to a station curve. Time-zone and measurement-window verification must precede a definitive hourly comparison.

The support analysis identifies another uncertainty that is independent of prediction bias. Sparse or irregularly positioned receptors and highly unequal administrative polygons can change the apparent extent of priority areas. Voronoi accounting makes the translation explicit, but a different receptor design may still change the partition and concentration sampling. The candidate grid and the analytical origin tests address different parts of that problem and should remain distinguished. The new coordinates do not yet carry newly simulated concentrations. The neighbourhood analysis also ends at the municipal support boundary, so edge patterns require a future check with an external analytical buffer.

The near-zero-area records also require a cartographic decision before final policy integration. They should be traced to the original zoning geometry and its topology, with municipal technical review where necessary. Keeping their identifiers avoids losing the link to the administrative dataset. However, reporting them alongside ordinary polygons without a support flag would conceal a material difference in interpretation. Their small area has little influence on municipal area totals but can strongly affect counts of classified units.

## Municipal application and health extension

The proposed deliverable to municipal planning is a table and map series identifying relative concentration patterns, locally associated regions, received group contributions and the shares of each zone overlapping those patterns. Such information can guide the location of additional monitoring, verification of activity schedules and source-control scenario design. It is an orienting technical product whose interpretation remains with the competent public authorities.

Population refinement should follow the same distinction between analytical support and administrative reporting. Census totals need residential evidence before being assigned to small receiving regions, particularly in extensive rural polygons. Subsequent health scenarios can compare annual reference levels for PI-2, PI-3, PI-4 and PF using a verified response function and compatible baseline event rates. Until those inputs are available, a relative health fraction must not be reported as a number of locally observed or preventable deaths.

## Temporal support in management regionalization

The contrast between complete and persistent-direction daily scenarios shows that temporal selection is part of the regionalization problem. Affinity-zone and regional-boundary studies provide a basis for examining environmental patterns before administrative aggregation (Vienneau and Briggs, 2013; Liu et al., 2018; Akhtar and Han, 2026). Here, the complete-meteorology reference adds a way to test whether a targeted episode subset preserves that spatial description. Directional envelopes support source investigation under identifiable meteorological conditions, while the unconditioned reference prevents those conditions from being mistaken for the whole distribution. This contribution concerns the traceability and conditional reliability of the classification. It does not establish causal transport paths or remove the remaining emissions and model-performance uncertainty.
